title: Mate Security Crosses $50M in Funding as AI Security Operations Startup Heads to Black Hat USA
excerpt: Artificial intelligence is reshaping cybersecurity at a pace that many security operations centers were never designed to handle. While organizations are embracing AI to improve efficiency, attackers are also using the technology to increase the speed, scale, and sophistication of cyberattacks. The result is growing pressure on enterprises to rethink the foundations of security operations […]
content_html:
TL;DR

Mate Security has closed a $35M Series A led by Canaan Partners with Insight Partners, Team8, and M12. Total funding now exceeds $50M, less than a year after stealth. The company’s bet is that AI security agents need organizational context, not just alert data, to make trustworthy decisions. It reports 500%+ growth since Q3 2025 and will exhibit at Black Hat USA 2026.

Artificial intelligence is reshaping cybersecurity at a pace that many security operations centers were never designed to handle. While organizations are embracing AI to improve efficiency, attackers are also using the technology to increase the speed, scale, and sophistication of cyberattacks. The result is growing pressure on enterprises to rethink the foundations of security operations rather than simply adding more automation.

That backdrop has helped drive momentum for Mate Security, which announced a $35 million Series A funding round, bringing the company’s total funding to more than $50 million less than a year after emerging from stealth. As first reported by Axios, the investment was led by Canaan Partners, with participation from Insight Partners, Team8, and M12, Microsoft’s Venture Fund. The company says the new capital comes as adoption accelerates among Fortune 500 organizations seeking an AI-native approach to security operations.

Building Security Operations Around Context

Founded by veterans of Wiz and Microsoft, Mate argues that one of the biggest challenges facing today’s security teams is not simply alert volume, but the inability to trust AI-generated outputs without sufficient context. While many AI-powered security tools promise faster investigations, analysts still need confidence that recommendations are accurate before taking action.

Mate’s platform addresses this challenge by creating what it describes as an organizational context layer that allows AI agents to understand how a business operates before making security decisions. Instead of relying solely on alerts, the platform incorporates business knowledge into investigations to improve accuracy and reduce unnecessary escalations.

For example, a burst of suspicious login attempts may initially appear malicious. However, if the system understands that an internal security test was scheduled during that period, it can identify the activity as a likely non-threat. Similarly, file downloads by an employee can be evaluated alongside organizational context such as personnel changes or document classifications before determining whether they represent genuine risk.

The company’s platform is designed around an open architecture that allows specialized AI agents to detect, investigate, respond to, and hunt for threats while operating from the same governed context.

Growth Follows Enterprise Adoption

The latest funding follows an oversubscribed $15.5 million Seed round announced only eight months ago. According to the company, participation from all existing investors helped bring total funding above the $50 million mark.

Mate also says it has experienced significant commercial momentum, reporting growth of more than 500% since the third quarter of 2025 as Fortune 500 enterprises increasingly adopt its agentic security operations platform.

“When we started Mate, we knew we had to invest in the foundation: context and trust, and build them deeply into our product,” said Asaf Wiener, CEO and Co-Founder of Mate Security. “We brought in some of the best AI builders and security experts, and I’m excited to see how well this approach is being received by the market. We will continue moving fast and stay laser-focused on our customers, as we expand into new markets and categories to build the Open Security Operations foundation of the future.”

The company says its platform enables AI security operations through a centralized Security Context Graph that collects, resolves, and maintains organizational knowledge. AI agents then operate using that governed context while trust mechanisms enforce permissions, quality, coherence, and auditability across investigations and response activities.

Investors See a Shift in Security Operations

Investors backing the company view the technology as part of a broader shift in how enterprise security teams will operate as AI becomes increasingly embedded in both offensive and defensive cybersecurity.

“AI is forcing a fundamental rethink of security operations. What stood out to us about Mate wasn’t simply its use of AI; it was the team’s conviction that trustworthy AI requires a deep understanding of how an organization operates,” said Joydeep Bhattacharyya, General Partner at Canaan. “By building a shared context layer that gives AI agents that understanding, Mate has taken a fundamentally different approach to security operations. The customer feedback and success we’ve seen in competitive evaluations reinforce our belief that the team is solving an important problem in a differentiated way.”

Insight Partners also pointed to operational trust as a key differentiator.

“Security operations was not built for the speed or scale of modern AI-driven attacks,” said Teddie Wardi, Managing Director at Insight Partners. “Mate is doing something few security companies have managed: combining genuine AI depth with operational trust to rebuild security operations for the AI era. We are proud to support a team that consistently outexecutes.”

Team8 and M12 similarly highlighted the company’s rapid execution and open AI architecture as organizations seek flexibility when adopting emerging AI technologies for cybersecurity.

Black Hat Appearance

The newly announced funding comes just ahead of one of cybersecurity’s largest annual gatherings. Mate Security will exhibit at Black Hat USA 2026, taking place from August 3–6, where the company will be located at Booth 4717.

With fresh funding, continued enterprise adoption, and a growing focus on AI-native security operations, the company is positioning itself around a central premise: that effective AI security depends not only on powerful models, but on giving those models the organizational context needed to make decisions security teams can trust.

blocks.html_en: With fresh funding, continued enterprise adoption, and a growing focus on AI-native security operations, the company is positioning itself around a central premise: that effective AI security depends not only on powerful models, but on giving those models the organizational context needed to make decisions security teams can trust.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

Mate Security 已完成由 Canaan Partners 领投、Insight Partners、Team8 和 M12 领投的 3500 万美元 A 轮融资。 目前融资总额已超过 5000 万美元，距离秘密行动还不到一年。 该公司的赌注是，人工智能安全代理需要组织背景，而不仅仅是警报数据，才能做出值得信赖的决策。 据报告，自 2025 年第三季度以来增长了 500% 以上，并将参加 2026 年美国黑帽大会。

人工智能正在以许多安全运营中心无法应对的速度重塑网络安全。 虽然组织正在采用人工智能来提高效率，但攻击者也在利用该技术来提高网络攻击的速度、规模和复杂性。 结果是企业面临越来越大的压力，要求它们重新思考安全运营的基础，而不是简单地增加更多自动化。

这种背景帮助推动了 Mate Security 的发展势头，该公司宣布完成 3500 万美元的 A 轮融资，使该公司的总资金在走出隐秘不到一年后就超过 5000 万美元。 正如 Axios 首次报道的那样，该投资由 Canaan Partners 领投，Insight Partners、Team8 和微软风险基金 M12 参与其中。 该公司表示，新资金的出现正值财富 500 强组织加速采用人工智能原生安全运营方法之际。

围绕上下文构建安全操作

Mate 由 Wiz 和 Microsoft 的资深人士创立，他认为当今安全团队面临的最大挑战之一不仅仅是警报量，而是在没有足够背景的情况下无法信任人工智能生成的输出。 尽管许多人工智能驱动的安全工具承诺更快地进行调查，但分析师在采取行动之前仍然需要确信建议是准确的。

欧盟科技的💜

来自欧盟科技界的最新传言、我们明智的创始人鲍里斯的故事，以及一些值得怀疑的人工智能艺术。 每周都会免费发送到您的收件箱中。 立即注册！

Mate 的平台通过创建组织上下文层来解决这一挑战，该层允许人工智能代理在做出安全决策之前了解企业的​​运营方式。 该平台不是仅仅依赖警报，而是将业务知识融入调查中，以提高准确性并减少不必要的升级。

例如，一连串可疑的登录尝试最初可能看起来是恶意的。 但是，如果系统了解在此期间安排了内部安全测试，它可以将该活动识别为可能的非威胁。 同样，在确定员工下载的文件是否代表真正的风险之前，可以与组织环境（例如人事变更或文档分类）一起进行评估。

该公司的平台是围绕开放式架构设计的，允许专门的人工智能代理在同一受控环境中运行时检测、调查、响应和寻找威胁。

企业采用后增长

最新一轮融资是在 8 个月前宣布的 1550 万美元种子轮超额认购之后进行的。 据该公司称，所有现有投资者的参与使总融资额超过了 5000 万美元。

Mate 还表示，随着财富 500 强企业越来越多地采用其代理安全运营平台，该公司经历了巨大的商业势头，自 2025 年第三季度以来增长了 500% 以上。

Mate Security 首席执行官兼联合创始人阿萨夫·维纳 (Asaf Wiener) 表示：“当我们创办 Mate 时，我们知道必须投资于基础：环境和信任，并将它们深深地融入到我们的产品中。” “我们引进了一些最优秀的人工智能构建者和安全专家，我很高兴看到这种方法受到市场的欢迎。 随着我们扩展到新的市场和类别，以构建未来的开放安全运营基础，我们将继续快速发展并始终专注于我们的客户。”

该公司表示，其平台通过集中式安全上下文图来收集、解析和维护组织知识，从而实现人工智能安全操作。 然后，人工智能代理使用受管环境进行操作，同时信任机制在调查和响应活动中强制实施权限、质量、一致性和可审计性。

投资者看到安全运营的转变

支持该公司的投资者认为，随着人工智能越来越多地嵌入进攻性和防御性网络安全中，该技术是企业安全团队运作方式更广泛转变的一部分。

“人工智能正在迫使我们对安全运营进行根本性的重新思考。 Mate 的突出之处不仅在于它对人工智能的使用，还在于它对人工智能的运用。该团队坚信，值得信赖的人工智能需要深入了解组织的运作方式。”嘉楠耘智普通合伙人 Joydeep Bhattacharyya 说道。 “通过构建一个共享上下文层，让 AI 代理能够理解，Mate 采取了一种根本不同的安全操作方法。 我们在竞争性评估中看到的客户反馈和成功增强了我们的信念，即团队正在以差异化的方式解决重要问题。”

Insight Partners 还指出，运营信任是一个关键的差异化因素。

Insight Partners 董事总经理 Teddie Wardi 表示：“安全运营并不是为了现代人工智能驱动的攻击的速度或规模而构建的。” “Mate 正在做一些安全公司无法做到的事情：将真正的人工智能深度与操作信任相结合，重建人工智能时代的安全操作。 我们很自豪能够支持一支始终表现出色的团队。”

Team8 和 M12 同样强调了该公司的快速执行和开放式人工智能架构，因为组织在采用新兴人工智能技术进行网络安全时寻求灵活性。

黑帽外观

新宣布的资金是在网络安全最大的年度聚会之一之前宣布的。 Mate Security 将在 8 月 3 日至 6 日举行的 Black Hat USA 2026 展会上展出，该公司的展位为 4717。

随着新的资金、持续的企业采用以及对人工智能原生安全运营的日益关注，该公司将自己定位于一个中心前提：有效的人工智能安全不仅取决于强大的模型，还取决于为这些模型提供做出安全团队可以信任的决策所需的组织环境。
